contributorNote: Borana / Oromo (Afaan Borana / Orma / Kigalla) vocabulary compiled from Rev. J. L. Krapf & Rev. C. W. Isenberg (1840 "An Imperfect Outline of the Elements of the Galla Language", 1842 "Vocabulary of the Galla Language", 1850 "Vocabulary of Six East-African Languages"), Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1844–1845), R. N. Cust (1883), E. C. Foot (1913), Prof. Alice Werner (1915), BFBS (1921), and Catherine Griefenow-Mewis (1996). Expanded and cross-verified with Commercially Permissive Datasets (Google Research SMOL/GATITOS Oromo/Borana (en_orm, CC-BY-4.0), Kaikki.org Oromo Machine-Readable Dictionary (1,245 headwords, CC-BY-SA-4.0), CLDF ASJP v20 BORANA_OROMO & WAATA (CC-BY-4.0), OLDI FLORES+ & SIB-200 (CC-BY-SA-4.0)).

entries.english: Akafed'e Dalle's 16-Verse Prayer after the War between Hambo and Hamaya (1845)

entries.english: Traditional Galla Morning & Evening Prayers to Waca (1845)

entries.pronunciation: ya wa-ca na-gan na bul-tshi-te na-gan na ol-tshi

entries.english: Munich Letters of Otshu Aga (Oct. 16, 1840) & Akafed'e Dalle (Oct. 21, 1840)

entries.english: Etymology of 'Galla' & Indigenous Autonyms (Oromo & Himata) vs. Neighbouring Peoples (pp. XX, 24, 57, 117, 200)
entries.translation: Galla (< gala 'to go home / seek one's home', referring to the c. 1735 migration) • Autonyms: Oromo (p. 24) & Himata ('orthodox believer', p. 200) vs. Zidama (Christians/Abyssinians), Awalini (Muslims), Wada (heathens), & Faqi (Falasha Jews, p. 117)

entries.english: Monotheistic Worship of Wacᵃ / Wacayo & Consecrated Assembly Trees (Refutation of Tree-Worship, pp. XXI, 31, 125, 131, 146–147, 157, 161, 168)
entries.translation: Wacᵃ / Wacayo (God / Heaven, omnipotent & omniscient) • Consecrated assembly shade trees (never worshipped as deities): wateza (Bruce's Wanzey, p. 147), lafto (lafto Michaila, pp. 31, 157), makaniza (p. 161), meeça (pp. 31, 131, 168), & ba (in Sibu, p. 125)
